units.translation: accusative of the pronoun ἵ, which see
accusative of the pronoun ἵ, which see

imperative of the verb čáw, which has passed into an interjection of astonishment, as grammarians call it, used by those who are amazed at unexpected things, either singly or, more frequently, doubled.
Thus ča placed outside the verse
whence I conjectured that ča had fallen out before the verse beginning τί χρήμα λεύσσω [what is this I see?] in Ch. 10.

where before the bacchiac verse was read ἆἆ ἔα ἔα [ah ah! ah ah!], I wrote da, deleting ča ča, which is shown to be correct by v. 566, where I restored da before the iambic trimeter for ἆ ἆ ἒ ἔ [ah ah! ah ah!], which is read in M, the letters ἒ ἔ [ah ah!] indicating the gloss ἔα ἔα [ah ah!] written beside ἆ ἆ [ah ah!].
Ah! What is this I see?
Ah ah! Indeed! How is it? How has it turned out in the house?
